UI_AMS_Help_Overview: What it does: Worn gear has a physical cost. Its weight, bulk, trapped heat and restricted breathing change how fast endurance drains and recovers, how fast sleep clears fatigue and how quickly you swing, all compared with wearing nothing. Protection and carry weight stay vanilla, and armor no longer builds discomfort: its bulk counts toward Load instead.

UI_AMS_Help_ExportTooltip: Save a support report with your loadout, burden calculations, mod list and game state.

UI_AMS_Help_Reading: Reading the tab: The top line is the one thing worth knowing right now. Each row names a cost and its pips show how strong it is. Hover a ? for how that row works, hover a row to see the gear behind it on the body map, and hover a body part to see what sits there.
UI_AMS_Help_Armor: Armor buttons: Take Off Armor moves your stiff gear into your inventory and remembers the set. Drop Armor puts it on the floor instead. Wear Armor puts exactly those pieces back on, from your bags or the floor next to you.
UI_AMS_Help_Tips: Tips: Sit down to recover, since weight never slows recovery while seated. Shed a layer when you run hot, take masks off when the air is clean, and take armor off before sleeping. Leg and foot armor costs the most for its weight.
UI_AMS_Help_Sandbox: Sandbox options: One scale sets how heavy gear feels overall, and the heat, breathing, arm strain and sleep effects can each be turned off.
UI_AMS_Help_Modded: Modded gear: Clothing and armor from other mods are rated automatically from their weight, slot and vanilla stats.
UI_AMS_Info_Load:
How heavy your worn gear is for your body.
- Each item counts its weight.
- Legs, feet and arms count up to twice as much: you lift them with every step and swing.
- Stiff or bulky gear adds extra.
- The first 3.5 kg, about a set of everyday clothes, is free.
- A heavier or stronger character carries the same kit more easily.
Every other row grows with Load.
UI_AMS_Info_Endurance:
What your gear does to endurance, compared with wearing nothing.
# Recovery
- Sitting: always normal.
- Standing: a little slower.
- Walking: much slower. Very heavy loads drain even at a walk.
# Exertion
- Running and sprinting drain faster the heavier you are.
Values preview each pace with your current gear, heat and breathing.
UI_AMS_Info_Heat:
Insulating gear traps body heat.
- It only counts once you are actually running hot.
- Then recovery slows by up to half, even sitting down.
- Exertion costs more too.
- Cool off or shed a layer and it fades within minutes.
In the cold the same gear just keeps you warm, with no penalty.
UI_AMS_Info_Breathing:
Masks, respirators and sealed suits restrict airflow.
- Resting and walking are free.
- The harder you work, the more extra endurance it costs.
- The full rating applies at a sprint.
A filtered gas mask is the worst. Take it off when the air is clean.
UI_AMS_Info_Melee:
Gear on your shoulders, arms and hands moves with every attack.
- Swings are %1 slower per kilo, up to %2.
- Heavy arm gear makes your arms stiffen faster in a long fight.
- Chest and leg armor do not touch your swing.
UI_AMS_Info_Sleep:
Stiff gear makes sleep clear fatigue more slowly.
- About %1 slower per kilo, up to half.
- Torso armor counts fully, limb armor partly, headgear not at all.
- Soft clothes are fine.
Take Off Armor before bed, Wear Armor when you wake up.
UI_AMS_Info_Gear:
The worn items that add the most load, heaviest first.
- Cells rate a single piece.
- Hover a row to see where it sits on your body.
- When one piece makes the difference, the line below says what taking it off would change.
